newsitem.title: GERMANY: Palm says fundamentally opposed to EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Palm says fundamentally opposed to EMU delay.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Guntram Palm said on Tuesday he was fundamentally opposed to delaying European monetary union from the planned start date on January 1, 1999.

"I am fundamentally against a delay because I believe it would bring absolutely no advantage. I think that in one or two years we would be left in the same situation but perhaps in an even worse environment," he said.
Palm also said it was important to have precise goals for entry into European monetary union, but said the room for flexibility in the Maastricht Treaty should be used.
"Precise goals are important for discipline. Removing those goals would lead to a loss of orientation and I believe one should use the freedom that is given," Palm said.
Palm also said Germany would meet entry criteria in 1997, the year when finances are reviewed for membership, without using accounting tricks or one-off measures.
But Palm said he did not expect Germany to meet the targets precisely.
"We will fulfil the criteria. After all, we always place the greatest stress on having numerical goals," Palm said.
